questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify and explain the significance of the events that marked Jesus' arrest, trials and crucifixion, confirming him as the promised Saviour of the world.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In John's Passion narrative (chapters 18-19), Jesus is not a helpless victim but a king who is in control, and the events confirm that he is the Saviour promised in Scripture. The Samaritans already call him "the Saviour of the world" (4:42), and the Passion shows how he saves.

**1. The arrest (18:1-12).**
- It takes place in a garden across the Kidron valley, and Jesus knows all that will happen to him (18:4).
- When he says "I am he", the arresting party draws back and falls to the ground (18:5-6), showing his divine authority.
- He asks that his disciples be allowed to go (18:8-9), and he refuses to resist with the sword: "shall I not drink the cup that the Father has given me?" (18:11).
- *Significance*: he gives himself freely, and protects his followers.

**2. The Jewish trial (18:12-27).**
- He is taken to Annas and then Caiaphas, who had said that it was expedient that one man should die for the people (18:14; 11:50).
- He replies openly about his teaching (18:20-21), while Peter denies him three times (18:15-27).
- *Significance*: the leaders' unconscious testimony to his saving death; the contrast between the faithful Jesus and the failing disciple.

**3. The trial before Pilate (18:28-19:16).**
- Kingship is the main issue: "My kingdom is not of this world" (18:36); "You say that I am a king. For this purpose I was born... to bear witness to the truth" (18:37).
- Pilate three times finds no case (18:38; 19:4, 6). He has Jesus flogged, and the soldiers mock him with a purple robe and a crown of thorns, and Pilate presents him: "Behold the man!" (19:5) and "Behold your King!" (19:14).
- The chief priests say "We have no king but Caesar" (19:15), a rejection of Israel's hope.
- *Significance*: the true king is condemned by the world, and the world's judgment is reversed. Jesus is judge and not the judged.

**4. The crucifixion (19:17-37).**
- He carries his own cross (19:17). The title "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews" is written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek (19:19-20), proclaiming his kingship to all peoples.
- The soldiers cast lots for his seamless tunic (19:23-24), fulfilling Scripture (Psalm 22:18), and he entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple (19:26-27).
- "I thirst" (19:28) fulfils Scripture, and "It is finished" (19:30) shows that his work is completed. He "gave up his spirit".
- His legs are not broken, but a soldier pierces his side and blood and water flow out (19:33-35). This recalls the Passover lamb whose bones were not to be broken (Exodus 12:46), and links to "Lamb of God" (1:29). The death occurs on the day of Preparation of the Passover (19:14).
- *Significance*: Jesus is the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world, and the cross is his glorification (12:32).

**Conclusion.** The arrest, trials and crucifixion in John show Jesus as the sovereign, innocent and obedient Son, the king whose throne is the cross, and the Passover Lamb who gives life to the world. In this way they confirm that he is the promised Saviour of the world.
